Seminar Title:

Removal of Acetamiprid by solar-powered electrocoagulation (SPEC): Correlating the experimental results using response surface methodology

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Chemical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Manisha Priyadarshini Tripathy ( Rollno : 523ch1006)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Chemical Engineering Nre Seminar Room

Date and Time:

25 Sep 2026 4 pm

Contact:

Madhusree Kundu

Abstract:

Acetamiprid, a widely used neonicotinoid pesticide, is water-soluble and can enter aquatic environments through agricultural runoff and other pathways. In the present study, solar-powered electrocoagulation (SPEC) was investigated as a sustainable approach for the removal of Acetamiprid from aqueous solution. A laboratory-scale batch electrocoagulation system was developed using iron electrodes and a photovoltaic solar panel as the direct-current power source. The treatment performance was evaluated by varying important operating parameters, including applied voltage, treatment time, and initial Acetamiprid concentration. The solar-powered batch electrocoagulation process was successfully performed, achieving a maximum removal efficiency of 81% at an initial Acetamiprid concentration of 1000 ppb, neutral pH, 15 V applied voltage, and 30 min treatment time. Characterization of the electrocoagulated sludge by FTIR and XRD indicated changes in the physicochemical characteristics of the treated material and supported the association of Acetamiprid with the electrocoagulated floc through coagulation, precipitation, and adsorption processes. Overall, the study demonstrates the potential of solar energy-assisted electrocoagulation as an environmentally friendly and practical treatment approach for Acetamiprid-contaminated water, particularly where conventional electrical power may be limited.
